title: Huevos Rancheros for the Crew
subtitle: Crisp tortillas, ranchero sauce, and sunny eggs for a full hall.
description: Corn tortillas, fried eggs, ranchero sauce, and beans on a platter — Mexican breakfast classic scaled for ten with cilantro and lime on the side.

ingredients.name: black beans
ingredients.notes: 15 oz, drained and warmed with cumin

ingredients.name: queso fresco
ingredients.notes: crumbled, plus cilantro and lime wedges

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Huevos Rancheros for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Simmer ranchero sauce
steps.instruction: Sauté onion in oil over medium heat until soft, about 6 minutes. Add garlic and chipotle, cook 1 minute, then add tomatoes and adobo sauce. Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thickened enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Warm beans and prep line
steps.instruction: Heat black beans with a pinch of cumin and salt in a covered pot over low heat. Set up a griddle station with warm tortillas, sauce, beans, cheese, and cilantro so eggs can go straight to plates.

steps.title: Crisp the tortillas
steps.instruction: Heat a lightly oiled griddle or cast iron over medium-high until shimmering. Fry tortillas 30–45 seconds per side until crisp at the edges but still pliable in the center. Hold stacked and covered with a towel.

steps.title: Fry eggs to order
steps.instruction: Fry eggs in a thin film of oil over medium heat until whites are fully set (165°F) and yolks are runny or jammy. Season each egg with salt and pepper as it comes off the griddle.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Huevos Rancheros for the Crew onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: portion and serve
steps.instruction: Layer two tortillas per plate with beans and a generous ladle of ranchero sauce. Top each stack with two fried eggs, crumbled queso fresco, cilantro, and a lime wedge. Serve immediately while tortillas stay crisp.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Huevos Rancheros for the Crew — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Simmer ranchero sauce first—it holds warm on the back burner while the griddle handles tortillas and eggs.
Assign one cook to tortilla frying and another to eggs so nothing sits under a heat lamp getting rubbery.
Plate in batches of four; hold finished plates covered for no more than 3 minutes before the line clears.
cleanupNotes: Deglaze the sauce pot with hot water while still warm so tomato sugars do not cement to the bottom.
Wipe the griddle with a bench scraper and oil paper towels between egg batches to prevent burnt bits.
leftovers: Ranchero sauce reheats well covered on the stove; add a splash of water and fresh cilantro at service.
Chop leftover tortillas and eggs into a chilaquiles-style skillet bake with extra sauce for the next shift.
